
# Load the data file 
The data is from https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AZvf5EuWStJ-gfY8z_AKUS2i5lRqNUyYWuTTx-pJe2Y/edit?gid=0#gid=0

# Make a histogram of the Weight of the students

```{r histogram-of-weight}
# With R base
hist(ieap2025$Weight,
     main = "Histogram of the Weight of the students",
     xlab = "Weight (kg)",
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "black",
     breaks = 10)  # nombre de classes

```
```{r}
# With ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Weight)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Weight",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
# With R base
ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Weight)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density Plot of Weight",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
# With ggplot2
ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Weight, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density of Weight by Gender",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("M" = "blue", "F" = "pink"))

```
```{r}
# With R base
boxplot(ieap2025$Weight,
        main = "Boxplot of Weight",
        ylab = "Weight (kg)",
        col = "orange",
        border = "black")

```
```{r}
# With ggplot2
ggplot(ieap2025, aes(y = Weight)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "orange", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Weight",
       y = "Weight (kg)") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Gender, y = Weight, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Weight by Gender",
       x = "Gender",
       y = "Weight (kg)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("M" = "blue", "F" = "pink")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Make a boxplot of the Weight of the students

```{r boxplot-of-weight}
boxplot(ieap2025$Weight
        , main = "Boxplot of the Weight of the students"
        , ylab = "Weight (kg)"
        , col = "orange"
        , border = "black"
        )
```
### 3.3 Boxplot to summarize the distribution

- **Main elements of a boxplot:**
  - Median (Q2) → line inside the box
  - First quartile (Q1, 25th percentile) → bottom edge of the box
  - Third quartile (Q3, 75th percentile) → top edge of the box
  - Interquartile range (IQR = Q3 − Q1) → spread of the middle 50% of data
  - Whiskers → extend to smallest/largest values within 1.5 × IQR
  - Outliers → points beyond the whiskers

- **Why start with a boxplot for an unknown distribution:**
  - Summarizes key statistics (median, quartiles, spread, extremes)
  - Shows asymmetry or skewness in the data
  - Detects potential outliers
  - Compact summary suitable for small or large datasets
  - Requires no assumptions about the distribution (robust for unknown distributions)

- **References for further reading:**
  - [Boxplot – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_plot)
  - [Understanding Boxplots – Towards Data Science](https://towardsdatascience.com/understanding-boxplots-5e2df7bcbd51)
  - [R Boxplot Documentation](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/graphics/versions/3.6.2/topics/boxplot)

# Make a scatter plot of Height vs Weight
```{r scatter-plot-height-weight}
      plot(ieap2025$Height, ieap2025$Weight
     , main = "Scatter plot of Height vs Weight"
     , xlab = "Height (cm)"
     , ylab = "Weight (kg)"
     , col = "purple"
     , pch = 19)
```

# Make a histogram of the Weight separating Males and Females
```{r}
# Histogram of weight distribution by gender

ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Weight, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Weight by Gender",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("M" = "blue", "F" = "pink"))


```


```{r weight_by_gender_hist, echo=FALSE, results = TRUE}
# Histogram of the density of weight distribution by gender
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(ieap2025, aes(x = Weight, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, adjust = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Weight Distribution by Gender",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal() 


```
